17 Plaintiff PATRICIA A. MCCOLM, pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure
18 || section 391.8, hereby submits Application for Order to Vacate 1995 Prefiling Order and Remove
19 || Plaintiff/Petitioner from Judicial Council Vexatious Litigant List and in support declares:
20 1. Iam the plaintiff/petitioner in this Application to Vacate Prefiling Order and Remove
21 || Plaintiff/Petitioner from Judicial Council Vexatious Litigant List; a single entry thereon in instant
22 || case issued on December 15, 1995.
23 2. The statements herein are my personal knowledge and if called as a witness could and
24 || would testify competently thereto.
25 3. Twenty seven years have passed without an application pursuant to C.C.P. section
26 || 391.8 or legal cause to continue the painful stigma occasioned by prior order precipitated by
27 . |
28 1
 
|
1 }| undiagnosed medical conditions; in particular, Hashimoto’s Disease and Multiple Sclerosis that |.
2 || imposed diminished capacity.
3 4. Asa 76 year old qualified person with disability under the American’s With
4 || Disability Act with multiple progressive disabling and life threatening medical conditions, there
5 |] is an acute absence of the energy, cognitive function and ability to avoid effects of P.T.S.D. from
6 || efforts to cope with the continuing painful distress inflicted by openly malicious shunning, verbal
7 || and physical abuse making mean-spirited attacks on false assumptions from prior
8 || disinformation/fake news/ “malarkey,” to justify hostile refusal of services and intentional
9 || financial abuse/detriment; e.g. wrongful taking of money/supplies re defective work, sneering:
10 || “Too bad! You can’t sue me!” There is no point in trying. A former Trinity D.A. said he would
11 || NOT prosecute anyone for crimes committed against me because I was a “vexatious litigant.”
12 || The ability to obtain local medical, home/auto repair and other services, for necessities of life in
13 || this remote location; including access to the local food bank, is not available by reason of stigma.
14 || One mechanic who refused to work on my car, said he had called all the other repair shops to
15 || warn them not to work on my car because I was a “vexatious litigant.” It isn’t easy being a target
16 || for theft, financial abuse and denial of services; among other insults, from such classification.
17 5. After 27 years of not being removed from the “black list,” gives argument to the belief
18 | that any abuse and false assumption is justified where this class of persons is concerned. Being a
19 || “vexatious litigant” appears to be equally onerous for individuals in this class as was being a jew
20 || in Nazi Germany or even being a racial minority in this Country. Why must society always
21 || seem to have a need to create an underclass to target for abuse? All citizens should have equal
22 || civil rights!
23 6. The passage of time, change in circumstances and belated discovery of medical
24 || detriment preventing adequate accommodation of disability to avoid the harm imposed by the
25 || stigma show that ends of justice are now served by granting this belated good cause application
26 || to vacate this source of continuing misuse of the order to inflict unwarranted harm.
27
28 2
 
| :
j 7. On May 24, 2022, this Court kindly granted plaintiffs first application for new
2 || litigation in this court against PG&E. Applicant hopes to acquire representation by a San
3 || Francisco attorney in the matter; but is hampered by PG&E interference with counsel.
4 8. PG&E has repeatedly acted to take advantage of applicant by calling attention to the
5 || stigma related to being on the vexatious litigant list. When applicant pleaded with the San
6 || Francisco PG&E corporate land attorney, to respect her real property ownership rights; he stated:
7 || “You have no rights, you are a vexatious litigant,” slamming down the phone! Said attorney
8 || also dissuaded a lawyer from assisting applicant in trying to resolve the easement/damage issues
9 | with PG&E by comments about her as a “vexatious litigant.” Absent removal of name from the
10 || judicial council list, it appears that PG&E will continue to make it impossible to obtain counsel
11 || to protect this citizen’s constitutional property rights.
12 9. Your kind consideration of an accommodating fresh start by granting this good cause
13 || application for order vacating the 1995 prefiling order and removing plaintiff/petitioner from the
14 |) Judicial Council Vexatious Litigant List is very much appreciated.
15 I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the
16 || foregoing is true and correct.
